Start here

At a glance

  • This is a road-to-glory guide for Fortuna Düsseldorf in Football Manager 27: from the 3. Liga to a Champions League win.
  • Money is the wall. The transfer budget is £0 and you have about £11K p/w of spare wages, so the first window is free agents, loans and pre-contracts C.
  • Do the five day-one decisions below before you press Continue, then work down the Day-one checklist.
  • Sections run along the top. Read each one's summary first; open the tables only when you need a name or a number.
  • When your screen and this guide differ, trust the screen and note it in Open questions.

The save in five lines.

  • The club. Biggest reputation, stadium and crowd in the 3. Liga, second-largest wage budget (£128K p/w), squad valued only 8th of 20 C. See The club on day one.
  • The rules. Four under-23 players on every match sheet, possibly three non-EU players in the 20, a window that shuts on September 1, 2026 L. See Signing and league rules.
  • The rebuild. Four seniors out, twelve free agents in, Nikoloz Dadiani on a pre-contract for January 1, 2027. Five new starters, and the bill still ends under budget. See The rebuild.
  • The tactic. One pressing 4-3-3 turned up twice: Front Foot, then Swarm, then Heavy Metal. You move up by feel. See Three tactics, one identity.
  • The climb. Six phases, about ten to twelve seasons on the fast path and fifteen to twenty on the slow one (planning figure U). No takeover money under 50+1, ever L. See Road to glory.

How this guide works

At a glance

  • Thirteen tabs along the top, left to right in the order you need them. The left and right arrow keys move between them.
  • Tap or click a table row to open its Details.
  • Every factual line carries a confidence tag. Money is in pounds per week.
  • The guide gives no advice on leagues to load, database size or hardware: those are your own set-up.

Moving around. Start, Rules, Club, Tactics, Staff, Rebuild, Wonderkids, Money, 3. Liga, Road, Checklist, Open questions, Sources. Every section and subsection opens with a short summary: read that first. The Tactics tab holds the tactics board, which shows all three stages slot by slot.

Tables. Where a table ends in a hidden Details column, tap or click the row to open it. Names, attributes, wages, clauses and fallbacks live there, so nothing recommended has been dropped.

Confidence tags.

Tag Meaning
C Confirmed for FM27: FMInside's FM27 database, an FM27 source, or your own game screens
L Likely: a real-life rule or fact the game should mirror ("in real life" in the sentence), or older-edition behaviour nothing in FM27 contradicts
U Unverified: one weak source, conflicting sources, or a judgement call. Check it in your save
(estimate) / planning figure My figure for planning, not a database number. Every free agent's wage ask is one

Ratings. "FMInside rating" is that site's own 0-99 score, not the game's 0-200 ability: Fortuna's best are 57-60, a 3. Liga starter is about 54, and 62 or more is above the division.

Money and units. All money is in pounds, wages per week ("£4.2K p/w"), converted from euros at 1.15 euros to the pound. Heights are in feet and inches, dates in US order (11/24/2026 in tables).

Signing and league rules

At a glance

  • Three rules shape the rebuild: four under-23 players on every match sheet, a £0 transfer budget, and a summer window that shuts on September 1, 2026.
  • Top two go up, third plays a two-leg play-off, bottom four go down.
  • Germany has no work permits and no 25-man list at this level. Sign who you like, then check the match-sheet limits.
  • No FM27 source shows the German rules screens, so most lines here are L. The last part lists the screens to read on day one.
  • Promotion removes the under-23 rule and brings a squad-quota rule instead. Start planning for that now.

Tags: C confirmed for FM27, L likely (real-life rule or older-edition behaviour), U unverified. "In real life" marks a rule taken from the real competition and not yet seen in the game.

The 3. Liga in one table

At a glance

  • 20 clubs, 38 games, no VAR.
  • First and second are promoted. Third meets the 16th-placed 2. Bundesliga club over two legs.
  • Seventeenth to twentieth are relegated to the Regionalliga.
  • The two reserve sides cannot go up; if one finishes in a promotion place, the next club takes it.
  • A top-four finish is also your ticket to next season's DFB-Pokal.
Item Rule Tag Details
Size 20 clubs, 38 matchdays C Club count is in FM Scout's FM27 data; 380 matches in real life
Automatic promotion 1st and 2nd L Real-life rule; expected unchanged in FM27
Promotion play-off 3rd v 16th of the 2. Bundesliga, two legs L Real-life rule. Play-off dates conflict between sources: see First-season dates
Relegation 17th to 20th go to the Regionalliga L Real-life rule
Reserve sides Stuttgart II and Hoffenheim II cannot be promoted L Long-standing DFB rule, not re-checked. They are also shut out of the DFB-Pokal
Tie-breakers Points, goal difference, goals scored, then head-to-head L Full real-life order: points, goal difference, goals scored, head-to-head, head-to-head away goals, away goals
VAR None U Real life: none, and clubs voted down a cheaper video system in February 2026. FM27 handling unknown
Licensing Not run by the game L Real life: yearly DFB finance check. 1860 München were refused for 2026/27 and Havelse kept the place; that swap is in the FM27 club list C. Insolvency costs 9 points in real life
Squad Cost Ratio Expect no such line here U FM27 added Squad Cost Ratio rules C; which competitions carry them is unpublished

Match sheet and squad rules

At a glance

  • At least four under-23 players must be on the sheet for every league game. They only need to be named, not played.
  • "Under-23" means born on or after July 1, 2003. In real life they must hold an EU (or EU-associated) passport; older FM editions said German.
  • Carry six or seven who qualify so that four are always fit.
  • Plan for at most three non-EU players in a matchday 20 until the rules screen says otherwise.
  • There is no squad list to register: a player is eligible once he signs.
Rule What to plan for Tag Details
Under-23 rule Four on every match sheet L Real life: DFB rule since July 1, 2025. Not yet 23 on June 30 before the season, and a national of an EU state or a country with an EU equal-treatment agreement. Assumed unchanged for 2026/27
Under-23 rule in FM27 Wording unknown U FM26 and earlier showed "four German under-23 players in the match squad". One report still describes the rule as "eligible for a German national team"; the DFB text above is the newer one. Read the rules screen
Where it applies League, DFB-Pokal, promotion play-off L Real life. It does not bind reserve sides, which have their own age limit
Non-EU players Assume a cap of three in the 20 U The DFB text read for this guide sets no number, only a valid residence permit. Older FM editions showed three. Check in game
Squad registration None L No 25-man list and no registration deadline of the English kind
Match squad 20 players: 11 plus nine substitutes L Not re-checked for 2026/27
Substitutions Five, in three stoppages plus half-time L Real-life rule; confirm bench size on the rules screen
2026/27 law changes Cosmetic at most U Real life: five-second countdown on goal kicks and throw-ins; ten seconds to leave when substituted; one-minute wait after treatment

Transfer windows and free agents

At a glance

  • The summer window closes on September 1, 2026 at 8:00 pm local time. That date is real; the opening date is a best guess.
  • Expect seven to eight weeks from the start date to rebuild.
  • Free agents can be signed all season, in and out of the windows.
  • Winter window dates for 2027 were not found. Read them in game before you plan January.

Loans

At a glance

  • Loans are how a club with no money borrows quality, but there is a cap.
  • Plan for six loans in and six out per season, and no more than three with any one club.
  • Under-21s and club-trained players sit outside the cap.
  • You already hold three loans: Andreas Müller, Lasse Rieß and Lukas Bornschein.
  • Stuttgart and Hoffenheim are less likely to lend to you: their reserve sides are in your league.
Point Rule or fact Tag Details
Cap, loans in Six per season L FIFA scheme adopted in Germany; the game applies a national cap where one exists. Check League Rules, Transfers
Cap, loans out Six per season L Same source
One club Three in and three out at most L Same source
Exempt Under-21s and club-trained players L So most loaned teenagers do not count
Loans already in Müller (Karlsruhe), Rieß (Mainz), Bornschein (Osnabrück) C FMInside shows all three as loans. Müller's and Rieß's parent contracts run to 06/30/2028 in FMInside's data, so neither can be approached for a free move this season
Wage share Negotiable L Any new loan wage has to fit inside the £11K p/w of spare budget L; how loan wages count is not published U
Squad risk Keep loans to a minority of the XI L They leave in June and the squad must be rebuilt again. Planning advice, not a rule

Who you can sign in Germany

At a glance

  • Germany has no work-permit system. Any nationality can sign.
  • The only limit on non-EU players is the possible match-sheet cap of three, which is unverified.
  • EU players at foreign clubs can join from age 16. Non-EU players can join only at 18.
  • German teenagers on youth terms move for a set compensation fee, not a negotiated one. That helps a club with a £0 budget.
  • Offer professional deals to your own best youth players so that rivals cannot do the same to you.

All rows are L: carried over from FM26 and real regulations, with no FM27 source to confirm them.

Foreign under-18s, EU Signable at 16 FIFA article 19 exception inside the EU and EEA
Foreign under-18s, non-EU Join on their 18th birthday A deal can be agreed earlier and dated forward
German under-18s Signable at any age shown Compensation fee replaces a negotiated fee when the player is on a youth contract
Youth contracts Youth terms until a professional deal Short professional terms from 16, standard contracts at 18
Training compensation Small at third-tier level Due when an under-23 signs a first professional deal or moves between countries. Budget a few tens of thousands of pounds for a foreign teenager

Clauses to use while money is tight

At a glance

  • With a £0 transfer budget, clauses are your currency.
  • Pay with money that only falls due after promotion or when a player plays.
  • Accept relegation release clauses; resist minimum-fee clauses.
  • These are recommendations, not rules.
Clause Do Why
Promotion wage rise, 15 to 25% Offer in place of basic wage Costs nothing until income has multiplied
Appearance, goal and clean-sheet bonuses Offer to older free agents Paid only when they play
Relegation release clause Accept Irrelevant if you go up
Minimum-fee release clause Resist If forced: foreign or higher-division clubs only, at three to four times value
Club option for one more year Add to every one- and two-year deal Protects value in players who develop
Sell-on percentage to the seller Offer in place of a fee The transfer budget is £0 C
Relegation wage drop Insert from the 2. Bundesliga on Insurance
Unused-substitute fee, large loyalty bonus Avoid Dead money
Team-of-the-year and cap bonuses Concede freely Rarely trigger at this level

The 50+1 rule and what it means for money

At a glance

  • Fortuna is a members' club. Members keep the voting majority, so nobody can buy control.
  • In the game that means no rich-owner takeover and no rescue money, ever.
  • Money grows four ways only: promotion, crowds, cup runs and player sales.
  • Do not wait for a takeover news item. If one appears in a German save, screenshot it.
Point Detail Tag
The rule In real life the parent members' club must hold most of the votes in the football company. Investors can own capital, not control L
Exceptions Leverkusen and Wolfsburg are long-standing exceptions; Leipzig and Hoffenheim are structured around the rule L
Fortuna A members' association with no outside investor found L
In the game Member-owned German clubs get no tycoon takeover; the board changes by election or routine change of chairman L
What to check Club Info or Board screen: ownership type, and whether "fan owned" appears U

DFB-Pokal

At a glance

  • You are in the 2026/27 cup as a club that played in the 2. Bundesliga last season.
  • Third-tier clubs are drawn at home in round one. In real life Fortuna drew SC Freiburg and lost 5-1.
  • Round one pays about £185K and each round roughly doubles it. Gate money is split evenly.
  • Next season's place needs a top-four league finish, or the Niederrheinpokal if the game has it.
  • One cup win is worth more than a season of your spare wage budget. Field the strongest XI.

How the rules change as you climb

At a glance

  • Promotion drops the under-23 rule and any non-EU cap.
  • From the 2. Bundesliga up, a squad quota applies: 12 German-licensed players, eight locally trained, four of them club-trained.
  • Club-trained means three seasons at Fortuna between 15 and 21. A player signed at 19 or older can never qualify.
  • So the teenagers you sign in the 3. Liga years are the ones who fill those places later.

European squad rules for later

At a glance

  • None of this applies until you reach Europe. Read it once now because it changes who you sign as a teenager.
  • UEFA's List A holds 25 players, and eight places are reserved for locally trained ones.
  • At least four of those eight must be club-trained; each one you lack shrinks the list.
  • Nationality is irrelevant: a foreign 17-year-old who stays three seasons is club-trained.
  • Top four in the Bundesliga is the Champions League place.

Real UEFA rules that the game has mirrored for years L. FM27 has the UEFA licence and registration screens L; update 27.1.0 fixed a Conference League registration bug C.

Rule Detail Details
List A 25 players at most
Locally trained places 8 of the 25 At most 4 may be association-trained: three seasons at any German club between 15 and 21
Club-trained The other 4 Three seasons, or 36 months, at Fortuna between 15 and 21
Shortfall Each missing player shrinks the list With no club-trained players the list is 21
List B Unlimited Under-21s with two unbroken years at the club since turning 15
Nationality Does not matter Only where the player trained counts
Squad cost rule Wages, amortised fees and agent fees capped at 70% of revenue plus sales profit Real UEFA rule. FM27 has Squad Cost Ratio rules C; scope and penalties are unpublished U
Places Top four: Champions League. 5th and the cup winner: Europa League. 6th: Conference League play-off Top four is confirmed in real life; the rest was not re-checked L
Extra place The two best associations in a season earn a fifth Champions League place Check the European places line on the table each spring L

The club on day one

At a glance

  • Fortuna are the biggest club in the 3. Liga with the squad of a mid-table one: top reputation, a 53,500 stadium, and a team valued 8th of 20.
  • You have £0 to spend on fees and about £11K p/w of spare wages. Every signing is a free agent, a loan, or paid for by an exit.
  • The squad can press through the middle (Hendrix, Müller, Wekesser) but it is slow: nobody has Pace above 15 and only one player has Stamina above 14.
  • Four contracts end on June 30, 2027 and three regulars are loanees. Zimmermann is the top earner at £10.0K p/w: he starts for now, and his wage is the first to free once a right-back arrives.
  • Read the Finances and Club Vision screens before you do anything: the balance, debt and board targets are not published anywhere.

Player numbers in this section are from FMInside's FM27 database (27.0.0, data patch 27.1.0), read on November 24, 2026 C. "FMInside rating" is that site's own 0-99 scale, not Football Manager's 0-200 ability. Club numbers are from FM Scout's FM27 pages C. Click a table row to open its Details.

What Fortuna is

At a glance

  • Relegated on the last day in May 2026; in the third tier for the first time in 17 years.
  • Highest reputation in the division and by far the biggest ground.
  • Wage budget 2nd in the league, team value only 8th. That gap is your job.
  • In real life the club did not go straight back up easily: it sat mid-table when the coach was sacked in October.
Fact Detail Tag
Division 3. Liga, 20 clubs. Top two go up; third plays the 16th of the 2. Bundesliga over two legs C / L
Reputation 1st in the 3. Liga. The number itself is not shown C
Stadium Merkur Spiel-Arena, 53,500 in game, the largest in the division by a wide margin C
Team value £12M, 8th in the league C
Average age 25.5, 14th C
Founded 1895 C
How they got here In real life they went down on the final day in May 2026 after losing 3-0 at Greuther Fürth, having used three head coaches in the season L
What was left In real life only six or seven second-tier professionals stayed; about 20 players arrived, nearly all free; more than half the club's employees were let go L
Crowd In real life: 19,000 season tickets (a 3. Liga record) and a 31,362 average by November 23, 2026, the best in the league L
The odds In real life only 11 of 49 clubs relegated from the 2. Bundesliga have gone straight back up L

The board

At a glance

  • The board's targets are not published. Expect promotion or at least the play-off place.
  • Write the expectation down at club selection and try to negotiate the league target down one step.
  • On day one ask for a senior affiliate and a coaching course. Do not ask for money or facilities yet.
  • Fortuna is a members' club under 50+1: no takeover and no rescue money, ever.
Topic What to expect Tag
League expectation Not published; check in game. Likely promotion or the play-off: top reputation, 2nd wage budget, and FM26 gave a 3. Liga favourite "gain automatic promotion" U / L
DFB-Pokal expectation Probably first or second round L
Club Vision culture items Not published; check in game U
Patience Not published. In real life the board dismissed the coach ten league games in U / L
Ownership A members' association. German member-owned clubs do not get tycoon takeovers in the series L

What the board will and will not allow on day one L:

Request Chance Note
Senior affiliate that lends players Best Costs the board nothing. Ask first
Coaching course for you Good Cheap; the board pays
Extra staff slot Fair The wage still comes out of your £11K p/w
Bigger wage or transfer budget Poor Retry after a cup win or a strong autumn
Training, youth facilities, youth recruitment, junior coaching Poor Revisit after promotion
Buy or expand the stadium No The city owns it

A refusal starts a cooldown of random length L. Make one request at a time.

Money on day one

At a glance

  • Transfer budget: £0. Every 3. Liga club starts on £0, so no rival in the division can outbid you.
  • Wage budget: £128K p/w, 2nd in the league, with about £11K p/w unused.
  • Bank balance, debt and the share of sale income you keep are not published: read Finances first.
  • The sources agree on the transfer budget and disagree on the spare wages. Trust your own screen.
Item FM27 value Tag
Transfer budget £0, joint 1st: all 20 clubs have £0 C
Wage budget £128K p/w, 2nd (Fortuna Köln £145K) C
Unused wage budget £11K p/w, the 3rd-largest headroom in the league C
Wage budget per year About £6.7M. In real life the squad budget was reported at about £6.5M C / L
Bank balance Not published; check in game. Expect a small positive or slightly negative figure U
Debt and loans Not published; check in game U
Share of sale income kept Not published for any FM27 club; read it on Finances before you sell anyone U
Moving money between budgets FM Scout says a slider on Finances moves money between the two budgets. Rate and limits are unknown; with £0 the only direction is wages into fees C / U
Stadium rent Fortuna rents the ground from the city. In real life the rent was reported as halved to about £1.3M a year for 2026/27. Expect a rent line on Finances L

Where the sources conflict:

Point The conflict What to do
Transfer budget No conflict. FM Scout's club page and its budgets article both say £0 C Plan on £0
Spare wages The budgets article says £11K p/w is unused C. One research report read the club page as fully committed at £128K L Read "available" on your own screen; plan on £11K at most
Wage period and currency The club page does not state the period. Top earners are shown in pounds per week, so the budget is read as £128K p/w L Confirm on Finances
Article against club pages The two FM Scout sources disagree for a few other clubs (Duisburg £95K against £117K). The article probably reflects the preview database L Treat rival budgets as approximate
Player wages FMInside's wages C are used in this guide. They sum to £73.9K p/w for the 20 first-team players with a published wage; six wages are not published The rest of the £117K is those six, the second team and possibly staff U

For scale C: Aachen £125K, Verl £114K, Wehen Wiesbaden £111K, Rostock £102K, Duisburg £95K, Essen £77K, Saarbrücken £74K. One division up the range is £102K to £602K p/w and a typical club has £190K to £250K p/w with £0.3M to £0.4M to spend.

Facilities

At a glance

  • Training 12, youth 12, youth recruitment 10, all out of 20. Mid-table 2. Bundesliga numbers that sit near the top of this league.
  • Nothing needs fixing in season one and the board will not pay for it anyway.
  • Junior coaching and any data or sports-science rating are not published: read Club Info.
  • First upgrade requests go in the week after promotion.

Target levels later L: training 14 to 15 by the 2. Bundesliga, 17 or more in the Bundesliga, 20 before a Champions League push.

Youth set-up and Fortuna II

At a glance

  • Fortuna II should sit in the fifth tier (Oberliga Niederrhein) and cannot go up while you are in the 3. Liga.
  • Fifth-tier football develops nobody over 19: loan those players out instead.
  • No affiliate clubs were found in any source. Ask the board for a senior one.
  • Arden and Slimani are the only youth products ready now.

The manager and staff in the database

At a glance

  • The database has Alexander Ende as manager. You replace him.
  • In real life he was dismissed on October 18, 2026 and Jens Langeneke took over; in the database Langeneke runs the second team.
  • The Director of Football in the database is Patrick Fabian, not Samir Arabi. Arabi is listed as Managing Director.
  • Full staff verdicts are in Staff on a budget.

Best XI today

At a glance

  • The stage 1 XI from Three tactics, one identity: Lord; Zimmermann, Oberdorf, Heintz, Wekesser; Hendrix; Consbruch, Müller; van der Sloot, Paulina; Schleusener.
  • It is picked for work, not rating: the ten outfield players average Work Rate 13.9 and Teamwork 13.8.
  • van der Sloot plays on the wing because the natural wide players (Gerezgiher, Slimani) do not press.
  • It is slow (average Pace 12.3) and four of the eleven are 31 or older. This is day one, before signings: the XI after the signings is in The rebuild.

At a glance

Built to press? Strengths and weaknesses

At a glance

  • Outfield averages: Work Rate 12.8, Stamina 12.5, Teamwork 12.0, Acceleration 12.2, Pace 12.7. Willing, not fit, not fast.
  • The stage 1 XI lifts Work Rate to 13.9 and Teamwork to 13.8, with Stamina 13.0, Acceleration 12.3 and Pace 12.3. Still short of what a full gegenpress needs.
  • Strong: the central midfield, the left side, height at centre-back, set-piece delivery.
  • Weak: pace everywhere, stamina outside Hendrix, pressing from the wide forwards, finishing, and a goalkeeper who does not come off his line well.

Under-23 players for the match sheet

At a glance

  • It only bites if you sell or loan several at once. Keep six or seven in the first-team group.

What this means

At a glance

  • Three conclusions to carry into Three tactics, one identity, The rebuild and Money and wages.
  • Start simple: the squad has the will to press but not the legs.
  • Pay for the rebuild with exits: three leavers turn £11,000 p/w of room into £29,345 p/w.
  • Protect Arden, Slimani and the under-23 group, and renew Oberdorf now.
  • Start simple and central. The squad has the will to press (Work Rate 12.8) but not the legs (Stamina 12.5, Pace 12.7). The first tactic is built around Hendrix, Müller and the left side; keep the defensive line modest until a quicker centre-back partnership and a keeper who comes off his line are in. See Three tactics, one identity.
  • The rebuild is paid for by exits, not by the board. Zimmermann (£10,005 p/w, once his replacement is in), Förster (£4,170) and Schleusener (£4,170) free £18,345 p/w; with the £11,000 spare that is £29,345 p/w, plus Benger's wage, which is not published. Only if a club takes them: Sauck (£3,335), van der Sloot (£5,217), Gerezgiher (£2,501) and Consbruch (£3,335) add £14,388 for £43,733, and sending Rieß back adds up to £6,670 for up to £50,403. Plan on about £29K p/w. Spend it first on a right-back who can both run and defend, a centre-back, a running midfielder, a right-sided forward who presses, and a striker who finishes. See The rebuild and Money and wages.
  • Protect what will be worth money. Renew Oberdorf now, keep Arden and Slimani out of any sale, plan for Müller going back to Karlsruhe (his own contract there runs to June 30, 2028), and keep six or seven under-23 players in the group so the match-sheet rule never picks your team for you.

Three tactics, one identity

At a glance

  • You build one attacking, pressing 4-3-3 and turn it up twice: "Front Foot", then "Swarm", then "Heavy Metal".
  • The eleven slots never change, so a player you sign for stage 1 still has a job at stage 3.
  • Stage 1 fits the squad you inherit. Only four outfield players have the legs for stage 2 today, so the rebuild decides when you move.
  • You move up by feel. Each stage lists what it looks like when it works, when it strains, and when the squad is ready for more.
  • Every role, instruction, option, style and formation name here was read from your own game on November 16, 2026 C. Which option to pick is advice.

Pick a stage at the top of the board, flip between in and out of possession, and click a slot to see its role, who plays it now and what to recruit. The board shows the squad on day one, before any signing; the XI after the signings is in The rebuild. The instruction lists show every setting at every stage beside the Gegenpress preset.

The idea in one screen

At a glance

  • What never changes: 4-3-3 DM Wide on the ball, a high block, direct passing, quick breaks.
  • What grows: how many players chase, how soon they chase, and how much each role has to think.
  • Stage 1 has one pressing role, stage 2 has three, stage 3 has four plus wide forwards who stay high.
  • Patch 27.1.0 (November 17, 2026) made pressing better coordinated and stronger in wide areas, which helps all three stages C.
What Stage 1 Front Foot Stage 2 Swarm Stage 3 Heavy Metal
Style to start from Clean Slate Gegenpress Gegenpress
In possession 4-3-3 DM Wide 4-3-3 DM Wide 4-3-3 DM Wide
Out of possession 4-1-4-1 DM 4-1-4-1 DM 4-3-3 DM Wide
Mentality Balanced Positive Positive
Pressing roles off the ball 1 3 4
Defensive Transition Standard Counter-Press Counter-Press
Trigger Press Standard More Often More Often
Player instructions you add None None, or one Two to four
Squad it is written for 3. Liga 2. Bundesliga Bundesliga and Europe

The same four settings hold at every stage: Line of Engagement on High Press, Defensive Line on Higher, Passing Directness on More Direct and Attacking Transition on Counter-Attack. That is the identity. Pressing Trap stays on Balanced and Tackling on Standard throughout.

Why not start at stage 3: Sports Interactive's own example of something too complicated for lower-league players is relentless counter-pressing C. Complex set-ups take time and have a higher ceiling; simple ones work quickly with limited potential C. Why the destination is worth it: the Gegenpress preset was the best-scoring preset in testing before the patch and the steadiest after it C. All of that testing used top-flight squads; nobody has published an FM27 test on a third-tier side U.

Stage 1: "Front Foot"

At a glance

  • Stand high, press when the ball comes near, break quickly, and ask nobody to do anything clever.
  • Create New Tactic: Clean Slate, then 4-3-3 DM Wide, then 4-1-4-1 DM. Mentality Balanced.
  • Only four team instructions leave the middle option. No player instructions.
  • The current squad can play it now: eight of the eleven first choices meet every stage 1 minimum for their slot (Lord, Consbruch and van der Sloot each miss one or two).
  • Heintz is the risk. He has Pace 11 and Acceleration 10 behind a Higher line C.

What to set. Press the "+" beside the tactic dropdown.

Step Pick Why
1. Tactical Style Clean Slate "Create your own tactical style": the fewest instructions to learn
2. Formation - In Possession 4-3-3 DM Wide One striker, three midfielders: the squad is deepest in midfield
3. Formation - Out of Possession 4-1-4-1 DM A flat four with a screen behind it covers the full-backs
Mentality Balanced The high block already puts you on the front foot
Slot dropdown Primary Trained Tactic Train this and nothing else at first

Nobody has opened Clean Slate in your game, so its starting values are U. I assume the middle option everywhere. Check all 28 settings against the board once, then leave them.

The research left one question open: whether to mirror the tactic so the right-back attacks. The numbers answer it. Keep it as drawn: Wekesser is a real attacking left-back and Zimmermann a real holder, while van der Sloot's defending numbers make him a winger.

Four senior players miss the stage 1 running floor (Work Rate, Stamina, Acceleration and Pace all 11 or more) C: Heintz (Acceleration 10), Benger (Acceleration 9, Pace 9), Förster (Work Rate 10) and Gerezgiher (Work Rate 10). Use them knowingly.

What it feels like. Opponents start their attacks from their own third and go long early. You win second balls in their half through numbers, not chasing. Chances come from quick breaks down the left and crosses from the right. Possession sits around half or a little under, and that is fine.

Signs it is working.

  • Their goalkeeper and centre-backs hit it long without being chased.
  • Consbruch or his cover arrives in the box beyond the striker.
  • Most of the front six finish with condition to spare.
  • The staff note on the Tactical Effectiveness tab stops asking for basics.

Signs of strain, and the fix inside the tactic.

  • Balls over the top for a runner against Heintz: Defensive Line to Standard for that match.
  • The striker never touches the ball: Target Forward, with GK Distribution (target) on Target Forward.
  • A large gap between midfield and defence when they play through you: Line of Engagement to Mid Block for the rest of that match. That still counts as stage 1.
  • Players in the red by the hour: that is a Stamina problem in the squad, not a tactic problem. Use the bench.

You are probably ready for stage 2 when these feel true, not when a number says so:

  • You are regularly the side with more of the ball in their half, and it feels like the team could do more.
  • The team finishes matches fresh, including the full-backs and both No. 8s.
  • You have two running No. 8s and a right-back who can attack and defend.
  • At least one centre-back can win a foot race.

Stage 2: "Swarm"

At a glance

  • Same shape. The team now hunts the ball the moment it is lost, and both full-backs join the attack.
  • It is the Gegenpress preset with the running turned down: eight settings softened, three pressing roles instead of the preset's two.
  • Six team instructions and seven roles change from stage 1. Mentality goes to Positive.
  • Only Müller, Wekesser, Risch and van der Sloot clear its running floors today C. This is the tactic for the rebuilt squad.
  • The style card's own warning applies from here: very tiring, and less control.

What to set. There are two routes to the same tactic. The style is only a foundation with full freedom to personalise C, so the end state is identical.

Route How Good for
Edit in place (recommended) Use Save in the slot dropdown to keep a copy of Front Foot. Then change the seven roles and six instructions below by hand, and set Mentality to Positive Keeps the Tactical Understanding the slot has built
Build new "+", then Gegenpress, 4-3-3 DM Wide, 4-1-4-1 DM. Soften the eight preset settings in the table. Set the roles A clean start, for example in pre-season

If you edit in place, leave the Style dropdown alone. Whether changing it overwrites your instructions was not read in your game U. Then Load the saved Front Foot into a second slot as your calm option. How much understanding a second slot shares with the first is U.

The game sets the Gegenpress default Mentality by squad strength: Positive at United, Balanced at Brentford C. Expect Balanced or lower for Fortuna L and set Positive yourself. If Positive feels loose, Balanced with everything else unchanged is still stage 2.

What it feels like. Long spells in their half. The ball comes back within a few seconds of losing it, often straight into a shot. Their goal kicks go long because the short option is covered. More shots, more corners, and more of your condition bars in orange at full time.

Signs it is working.

  • Regains high up the pitch turn into chances without a build-up.
  • Both Wing-Backs show up among your creators.
  • The staff note stops naming Pressing Intensity.

Signs of strain, and the fix inside the tactic.

  • One pass beats the press and three of yours are out of the game: left M(C) back to Central Midfielder off the ball. It is usually tired legs or low Anticipation and Decisions in the No. 8s.
  • Several starters have not recovered by the next match: play Front Foot for the midweek game.
  • Yellow cards for late challenges: check Aggression against Decisions in the pressing roles before blaming the tactic.
  • The right flank opens when the Pressing Full-Back jumps and misses: step him down to Full-Back.
  • Legs gone and no substitutes left: Trigger Press down one notch, then Defensive Transition to Standard.

You are probably ready for stage 3 when:

  • Swarm feels comfortable in most league games and the squad finishes fresh.
  • You have two centre-backs who win foot races and a goalkeeper who sweeps.
  • Both full-back slots have two players each who can run all day.
  • You are no longer the side being countered. Opponents sit in, and you want to pin them.

There is no harm in a whole season of Swarm in the 2. Bundesliga. The step to stage 3 depends on centre-back pace more than on league level.

Stage 3: "Heavy Metal"

At a glance

  • The full gegenpress: wide forwards stay high off the ball, both full-backs jump, the line steps up, the front three play narrow.
  • Create New Tactic: Gegenpress, 4-3-3 DM Wide, 4-3-3 DM Wide. Mentality Positive.
  • Five team instructions, six roles and the out-of-possession formation change from stage 2.
  • Tempo and Trigger Press stay one notch under the preset to protect condition.
  • Two off-the-ball role names were never read in your game. Pick them by behaviour tag, or use the fallback below.

What to set. Edit Swarm in place as before, saving a copy first. The one change you cannot make from the instruction lists is the out-of-possession formation. Where an existing tactic's formation is changed was not read in your game: look under Edit Tactic in the slot dropdown U. If you cannot find it, build new with the three picks above.

Instructions that change from stage 2.

Instruction Stage 2 Stage 3 Why
Attacking Width Standard Narrower The front three play close together
Supporting Runs: Overlap Balanced Overlap Both Flanks Wing-Backs go outside the narrow forwards
Defensive Line Behaviour Balanced Step Up More Squeezes the pitch for the press
Time Wasting Standard Less Often Keep the ball moving
Shots from Distance Balanced Discourage Wait for the better chance

Against the preset, Heavy Metal still softens Tempo (Higher, not Much Higher) and Trigger Press (More Often, not Much More Often). Four pressing roles add their own trigger, so the team presses hard without the top setting.

Slot Phase Stage 2 Stage 3 Details
GK On the ball Goalkeeper Ball-Playing Goalkeeper Starts counters. Only for a keeper who can pass; otherwise stay on Goalkeeper
D(C) right On the ball Centre-Back Ball-Playing Centre-Back One passer to break the first line; put it on the better passer's side
ST(C) On the ball Channel Forward False Nine Drops and links. If your striker is a runner, keep Channel Forward: change the role, not the player
D(L) Off the ball Full-Back Pressing Full-Back Both full-backs cover for wide forwards who no longer drop
AM(R) Off the ball Wide Midfielder Role tagged Stays High, Counter-Attacks First pass on the break. Name not read; check in game
AM(L) Off the ball Wide Midfielder Role tagged Tracks Back, Supports Defence The harder worker balances the outlet. Name not read; check in game

The fallback that uses only names you can already see: stay in 4-1-4-1 DM off the ball with Wide Outlet Wide Midfielder on the right and Tracking Wide Midfielder on the left. That gets most of the way there.

Player instructions. Add one at a time and watch Complexity after each.

Who Instruction Details
Both Inside Forwards Attack Box - Side and Attack Box - Depth Left forward to the far post, right forward near post or centre. Option labels not read, and they may be padlocked for the role U
Channel Midfielder Attack Box - Depth To arrive late
A centre-back with Dives Into Tackles Tackling, most cautious option Out of Possession tab L

What it feels like. The opponent cannot get out. Goals come in bursts after regains. Your full-backs are among your leading creators.

Signs it is working.

  • Opponents rarely complete a pass out of their own third.
  • The wide forward who stays high receives the first pass after a regain.
  • The Covering Centre-Back sweeps up long balls without a panic.

Signs of strain, and the fix inside the tactic.

  • One long ball beats eight players: Defensive Line Behaviour back to Balanced.
  • The Covering Centre-Back is in foot races all match: Defensive Line to Standard for that match.
  • A full-back is beaten after jumping: Pressing Full-Back to Full-Back on that side.
  • The team fades after the hour: use every substitution, and play Swarm for the next game.
  • Injuries rise in a crowded run of fixtures: Swarm until the run ends.

There is no stage 4. From here you improve the players, not the tactic. Swarm stays in the second slot as the calm version.

What the gauges should read

At a glance

  • Three gauges sit at the top right of the tactics screen: Intensity, Complexity and Effectiveness.
  • Intensity should climb a step with each stage; Complexity should start low and end High.
  • Only stage 3's readings are confirmed, from the Gegenpress card. Read the other two after you build them.
  • Change stages by editing the same tactic, so the parts that stay the same keep their understanding.
  • Clicking Effectiveness opens Training > Tactical Effectiveness.
Gauge What drives it C Stage 1 Stage 2 Stage 3
Intensity Press aggression, tempo, tackling style, mentality. Costs condition, raises injury risk Medium to High U High U Very High C
Tactical Complexity Team Instructions, Player Instructions, Opposition Instructions Low to Average U Average to High U High C
Tactical Effectiveness Tactical Understanding, Player Ability, Player Buy-In, Next Match Info Low start, climbs fast Dips, then climbs Dips, then climbs

If stage 1 reads the same Complexity whether you build it from Clean Slate or by softening Gegenpress, the starting style does not matter. Your opposition instructions count towards Complexity too, so go light on them while a stage beds in.

If Complexity reads higher than expected after a stage change, undo in this order: Shots from Distance, Time Wasting, GK Distribution (target), Short Goalkeeper Distribution, Supporting Runs. Keep Passing Directness, Counter-Attack and the pressing settings to the end.

The four parts of Effectiveness.

Part Key factors C What you can do
Tactical Understanding Eight Tactical Areas, plus Player Tactical Ability and Tactical Complexity Train the area the staff note names
Player Ability Player Capability, Player Role Suitability Recruit to the slot profiles
Player Buy-In Managerial Support, Teammates and Staff Relationships, Manager Tendencies Slow to move; keep the squad settled
Next Match Info Quality of Next Opposition Report, Opposition Player Knowledge Your own match planning

How understanding behaves when you change stage. The eight Tactical Areas are In Possession Shape, Passing Style, Build Up, Chance Creation, Out Of Possession Shape, Line of Engagement, Pressing Intensity and Pressing Trap C. Which instruction feeds which area is not published; the table is my reading U.

Move Should carry over Expect to retrain
Stage 1 to 2 In Possession Shape, Out Of Possession Shape, Line of Engagement, Pressing Trap Pressing Intensity (Counter-Press and the higher trigger); a little Passing Style and Build Up
Stage 2 to 3 In Possession Shape, Line of Engagement, Pressing Intensity, Pressing Trap Out Of Possession Shape (the new formation); a little Chance Creation

That is the reason for one shape throughout: each stage adds work to something the squad already knows. In testing before the patch, going from low to high understanding was worth about half a point a game, and training counted about twice as much as matches C. Patch 27.1.0 rebalanced how Tactical Effectiveness progresses, without saying in which direction C. Watch the bar, not the calendar.

Training to grow into it

At a glance

  • Training has seven tabs: Overview, Tactical Effectiveness, Individual Training, Mentoring, Training Intensity, Coach Assignments, Medical Centre.
  • One tactic in pre-season: Front Foot as the Primary Trained Tactic, nothing else.
  • Follow the staff note on the Tactical Effectiveness tab each week; it names the area that needs time.
  • Rotation is the biggest lever for a pressing side. Starting at 90% condition cost about 0.3 points a game in testing C.
  • Move up a stage in a one-game week or in the winter break.

Only the Tactical Effectiveness tab was opened in your game. What the other tabs are for is inferred from their names, and session names, intensity settings and rest rules are U. Confirmed about FM27 training C: senior sessions are built around the next match, team cohesion and tactical understanding; Sports Interactive's own examples include training an intense pressing unit and pressing high; the screen shows physical load for this week and the weeks ahead.

1 Front Foot Shape first: In Possession Shape, Out Of Possession Shape, Line of Engagement. Then Passing Style Stamina and Work Rate for the No. 8s and full-backs; Pace and Acceleration for centre-backs Order of areas is U; the staff note decides
2 Swarm Pressing Intensity will drop when Counter-Press arrives; train it first Anticipation and Decisions for the pressing roles; Finishing for the right Inside Forward L
3 Heavy Metal Out Of Possession Shape, then Chance Creation Passing for the Ball-Playing Centre-Back and goalkeeper; First Touch and Technique for the False Nine U

In real life the 3. Liga allows five substitutions and requires four under-23 EU or EU-associated nationals on the match sheet (see Signing and league rules) L. Confirm both on the competition's rules screen. Two players per slot is enough with one game a week: 20 outfield players and three goalkeepers U.

When What to do Tag

Set pieces

At a glance

  • Set pieces are the cheap edge: in real life about a quarter of 3. Liga goals do not come from open play L.
  • You already have the people: Förster's Corners 16, two full-backs with Long Throws 15, and a 6'8" centre-back with Jumping Reach 18 C.
  • Build routines on Tactics > Set Pieces after the tactic exists. The screen labels below come from one FM27 guide, not from your game.
  • Two corner routines per side, one free-kick routine, a long throw, zonal defending. No more.
  • Do not pay a wage for a specialist set-piece coach at this level.

Keep the same centre-backs and striker in the same jobs across every routine. After a change of personnel, reopen the screen or use "Ask Set Piece Coach to Assign".

What the evidence is worth. One test with a top-flight squad averaged 8.5 set-piece goals a season using Staff Preference, coach-assigned jobs and Long Throw, against 4.0 for the untouched default [C, tiny sample]. No lower-league set-piece test exists for FM27 U. Set pieces do not appear in the game's own list of what drives Complexity L, so they are free to add at stage 1.

Is a set-piece coach worth a wage? Not at this level. No FM27 source tests coach-built routines against your own U. Build the routines once, give Set Pieces training to whichever coach has the best Set Pieces attribute, and hire a specialist only if the staff screen shows a dedicated slot that would otherwise sit empty U. Until then give the area to Zlatko Muhović, the assistant already at the club (Set Pieces 16), or to the free agent Ovid Hajou (43, Set Pieces 18) if you hire him as assistant [C numbers]. See Staff on a budget. Revisit in the Bundesliga.

In-match changes

At a glance

  • Three switches cover most matches: chasing, protecting and ten men.
  • Each one uses settings you already know from the stages, so nothing new has to be learned.
  • Make the change late. A higher Mentality from kick-off cost points in testing C.
  • Undo it when the game state changes back.
  • Opposition plans are yours; these are only the tactic's own fallbacks.
Game state Change Details
Chasing a goal late Mentality up one step; Time Wasting to Less Often; GK Distribution (Speed) to Distribute Quickly If you end up going long: striker to Target Forward and GK Distribution (target) to Target Forward. Last minutes only U
Protecting a lead late Switch to the previous stage's tactic At stage 1 there is no previous stage: Line of Engagement to Mid Block, Defensive Line to Standard, Time Wasting to More Often. Short Goalkeeper Distribution may not be offered under Mid Block, because it sits in the High Press category L
Ten men Line of Engagement to Mid Block; Defensive Line to Standard; Trigger Press down one notch; Defensive Transition to Standard; Mentality down one step Keep the back four, the screen and both No. 8s; give up the right wide player and leave Attacking Transition on Counter-Attack. This is my advice, not a tested finding, and how the game redraws the two formations with ten was not read U

FM27 also has match-screen Tactical Tweaks C. Their names were not read in your game, and running them from kick-off cost points on a pressing tactic in testing C.

At a glance

  • Buy athletes first: Acceleration and Pace topped the tested ranking, and Work Rate and Stamina keep a press alive C.
  • Each slot has three minimums: 3. Liga for stage 1, 2. Bundesliga for stage 2, Bundesliga for stage 3.
  • First purchases: a quick centre-back, two running No. 8s, a right-back who can do both jobs, a scoring right-sided forward, a striker.
  • All minimums are rules of thumb U. If the search finds nobody at the wage, drop the technical numbers by one before the physical ones.
  • Since 27.1.0 the Player Discovery and Scout position screens have a Tactical Effectiveness column C. Sort by it once the tactic is built.

Staff on a budget

At a glance

  • The free-agent market is far kinder to a third-tier club for staff than for players: 5-star fitness and possession coaches will listen.
  • Six hires change most: a fitness coach, a goalkeeping coach, a physio, a head of youth development, an assistant and a possession coach.
  • Send offers in this order: Häfelinger, Squizzi, Adabi, Gentner, Venus, Hipp, then Nister and one of Schumacher or Morgado.
  • Keep Gruev, Gross, Fabian, both analysts and most of the medical room. Replace Fynn Müller, Çiçem and Pluntke.
  • Staff wages are not published and nobody knows whether they share your £128K p/w budget: make the first four hires before the player signings use the spare £11K p/w.

Every person and number here was read from FMInside's FM27 database (27.0.0, data patch 27.1.0) on November 24, 2026 C. "FMInside ability" and "reputation" are that site's own 0-99 scales, not Football Manager's 0-200 ability. Star ratings come from FMInside's coach calculator, which the site itself labels a provisional estimate built on the FM26 formula, so every star figure in this section is L. Verdicts (Likely, Possible, Long shot, Out) are the realism review's judgement, not a tested result L. Click a table row to open its Details.

Short forms in the tables: TK (Tactical Knowledge), PM (People Management), Mot (Motivating), Auth (Authority), Det (Determination), WWY (Working With Youngsters), JPA and JPP (Judging Player Ability and Potential), Neg (Negotiating), Data (Judging Player Data), Rep (FMInside reputation).

How staff work in FM27

At a glance

  • The game shows staff attributes as words, not numbers. The numbers in this section come from the database.
  • Each role runs on two or three attributes: hire on those and ignore the rest.
  • Coaches are rated in stars for each of nine training areas; stars fall when one coach covers several areas.
  • Nobody has published the FM27 star formula, and no FM27 test shows how much coach quality matters. Treat it as a cheap, modest edge.

Words on the profile screen and what they mean C:

Word Number
Elite 20
Outstanding 18-19
Very Good 15-17
Good 12-14
Average 10-11
Competent 7-9
Reasonable 4-6
Unsuited 1-3

Head of youth development His personality and preferred formation tend to shape the intake L
Director of football Negotiating if he handles deals, then Judging Player Ability and Potential C
Technical director Judging Staff Ability and Negotiating L
Scouts Judging Player Ability and Potential; Adaptability abroad; Determination helps C / L
Analysts The data attribute (FMInside calls it Judging Player Data; other FM27 lists call it Data Analysis) and Tactical Knowledge C / L
Physio Physiotherapy: shortens recovery C
Sports scientist Sports Science: fitness and injury-risk management, and better Medical Centre reports C

How coaching stars work:

Point Detail Tag
Training areas Nine: Attacking Tactical, Attacking Technical, Defending Tactical, Defending Technical, Possession Tactical, Possession Technical, Goalkeeping, Fitness, Set Pieces C
Where you set them Training > Coach Assignments C
What drives stars The area's coaching attributes plus Authority, Determination and Motivating C
Formula Not published for FM27. Every star figure here is a calculator estimate L
Several areas A coach's stars fall when he covers more than one area. The size of the drop is not published C / U
Workload Too few coaches on an area is likely to raise workload and lower its rating L
Ceiling On FM Scout's FM27 list nobody outside Fitness, Goalkeeping and Defending Tactical reaches 5 stars C
Rule of thumb in words Fitness or Goalkeeping at Very Good with the three mental attributes at Good is about 3.5 to 4 stars; Outstanding with Good is about 4 to 4.5 U
Growth Stars are current: coaches improve with badges and experience, so younger hires gain value C / L
You Your own coaching attributes are likely to count if you take part in training L
Does it matter? No FM27 test was found. Spend in this order: fitness and medical, goalkeeping, then the outfield areas U

Training itself changed in FM27: sessions now aim at carrying out the tactical plan for the next match, and load indicators show the physical cost for this week and the weeks ahead C. That is why the fitness and medical hires come first for a thin squad that presses.

Why reputation decides who comes

At a glance

  • A staff member weighs his own reputation against the club's before wages are even discussed.
  • Fortuna's FMInside reputation is 64, the highest in the division: people at about 65 or lower are within reach.
  • 66 to 72 is worth one offer. 73 and above is a long shot. 80 and above is out.
  • Only unattached people are recommended: you cannot pay compensation with a £0 transfer budget.
  • "Unattached" is a database status, not a promise. Look for the interested marker on the profile.
Staff reputation Verdict used here What to do
About 65 or lower Likely or Possible Offer. Expect a yes at a wage that fits, or a haggle
66-72 Possible at best One offer; have the fallback ready
73-79 Long shot Ask once if you like; plan without him
80 or more Out Do not spend the day on it

The bands are the realism review's reading of how the series behaves L; no FM27 source documents the rule. Fortuna's figure of 64 is quoted from that review and is not in the staff file, so confirm the club's standing on your own screen.

Other gates on a hire:

Gate What is known Tag
Role and ambition People take a job at or above their current title far more readily than a step down. A scout will take chief scout; a former head coach rarely accepts assistant L
Compensation Employed staff need their club's consent and often a fee. Assume you can pay none in season one L
Wage ceiling per role The board is likely to cap what each role can earn. The contract offer screen shows it L / U
Staff numbers Each category has a current and a maximum count. Fortuna's are not published; check in game U
Language No source states any effect. German speakers are a tie-break only U
Poaching Expect bigger German clubs to take your best finds once their badges rise L
Your assistant's suggestions Staff your own backroom suggests can be poor. Check the attributes yourself C

Finding your own lower-level staff

At a glance

  • You hire the second-team and under-19 staff yourself, and published lists stop at about 4 stars.
  • At this level 3 to 3.5 stars per area is respectable and is what your rivals have.
  • Search unattached and interested first, filter by the attribute words below, then sort by wage.
  • Prefer under-45s: they gain badges and improve.
Step What to do Tag
1 Staff search by role (Coach, Fitness Coach, Goalkeeping Coach); tick interested; contract status unattached L
2 Filter: the area attribute at Very Good or better; Tactical or Technical at Good or better; Determination, Authority and Motivating at Good or better C
3 For youth staff: Working With Youngsters, People Management and Motivating at Good or better, and a tactical preference that matches the first-team shape L
4 Then widen to employed staff at Regionalliga clubs, Bundesliga second teams and academies, Austria, Switzerland, the Dutch second tier and Scandinavia. Sort by wage, lowest first L
5 Prefer Professional, Resolute, Perfectionist or Model Citizen personalities L
6 Analysts: filter the data attribute at Very Good and sort by wage L

Day-one order, staff numbers and pay

At a glance

  • Do all staff business before you press Continue for the first time.
  • Read the limits first: how many of each role the board allows is not published anywhere. Check in game.
  • Offers into empty seats first, then replacements. End an incumbent's contract only once his replacement has agreed.
  • Make the first four hires before the player signings, in case staff pay shares the £11K p/w of spare wages.
  • No staff board request on day one. Ask for one more coach or scout seat after a good first month or two.

The rebuild

At a glance

  • Twelve free agents in, four seniors out, one pre-contract for January. That gives you five new starters and a wage bill that still ends under budget.
  • The transfer budget is £0 C, so nobody on the buy list costs a fee: the window is free agents, loans and pre-contracts.
  • Every attribute, rating, wage and contract date here was read from FMInside's FM27 database on November 24, 2026 C. Every wage ask is an estimate U.
  • Sign the first four inside the £11K p/w you already have spare, then spend each wage as it is freed.
  • The squad you inherit is audited in The club on day one; the roles and slot minimums are in Three tactics, one identity.

Term Meaning

Likely He should say yes at a wage that fits

The plan in one screen

At a glance

  • Out: Zimmermann, Förster, Schleusener and Benger. That frees £18.3K p/w in published wages, plus whatever Benger earns.
  • In: twelve free agents for about £24.1K p/w (estimate) U, and Nikoloz Dadiani on a pre-contract for January 1, 2027.
  • The bill moves from about £117K to about £122.8K p/w (estimate) U, against a budget of £128K C.
  • On day one: read three screens, offer Dadiani, open talks with the first four, then put the leavers on the market.
  • If Zimmermann will not move, stop at eight signings. If nobody moves, stop at four.

The sum: £117,000 less £18,345 plus £24,100 is £122,755. That leaves about £5.2K p/w under the budget, plus Benger's wage, which is not published. Dadiani takes about £2.0K of it in January (estimate) U. The budget and the £11K p/w spare are database figures C; read "available" on your own Finances screen before you trust them.

Day one, in this order:

  1. Read three screens before any offer. Finances: the wage room really available and the bank balance. The 3. Liga rules: whether there is a non-EU cap and how the under-23 rule is worded. The squad's contracts: the wages FMInside does not publish (Lord, Benger, Hottmann, Bouchama, Arden, Eixler).
  2. Offer Dadiani his pre-contract. His deal at Iberia 1999 ends on December 31, 2026 C, and other clubs are expected to ask.
  3. Approach the agents of N'Diaye, Gondo, Beifus and Kwateng. Together they come to about £9.8K p/w (estimate) U, which fits inside the £11K you have spare before anyone leaves.
  4. Offer out Förster, Schleusener and Benger. Offer out Zimmermann the moment Kwateng agrees, not before: he is your stage 1 right-back until then.
  5. Post loan adverts and ask Mainz 05 about Rieß. See Loans.
  6. As each wage clears, sign the next names on the list in order.

The window closes on September 1, 2026 L. Free agents can be signed after it closes, and their demands have historically fallen the longer they stay unattached L; neither is confirmed for FM27 U.

Who leaves and how

At a glance

  • Four seniors go first because they are too old or too slow for a press: Zimmermann, Förster, Schleusener, Benger.
  • Sell for nothing or loan with the wage paid. A release costs a pay-off from a bank balance you have not seen yet L.
  • Zimmermann is the hard one: 34 years old on £10.0K p/w C. Paying up his last year would cost about £520K, which a club with £0 cannot fund.
  • If he stays, you sign eight instead of twelve and keep him as right-back cover. His deal ends on June 30, 2027 C, so the wage frees itself.
  • Four more players are worth selling only if a club asks. Do not chase those deals.

Loans

At a glance

  • Nothing read for this guide shows who is loan-listed or what share of a wage a parent club pays. Every name here is a request to try, not a plan.
  • You already hold three loans: Müller, Rieß and Bornschein. Plan for a cap of six with under-21s outside it L; check the rules screen before a fourth.
  • A loan at this level adds depth and under-23 players, not starters: the young players at bigger clubs are mostly rated 45 to 55.
  • Offer no monthly fee and as little of the wage as you can. Promise playing time only where it is true.
  • Jordana of Girona B is the most useful name. Keep Müller and Bornschein; Rieß is not worth his wage.

How to ask:

Step What to do Tag
1 Player Search: Transfer Status set to listed for loan, Interested set to yes, age 18 to 23, sorted by your staff's rating for the role L
2 Post TransferRoom Requirements adverts with the transfer type set to loan L
3 Ask your Director of Football for loan suggestions and for advice on fee and terms C
4 Check Agent Offers every week; they grow towards the deadline C
5 Start with clubs that already lend to you or to this league in real life: Mainz, Karlsruhe, Osnabrück, Nürnberg, Kiel, Paderborn, Schalke, Hertha, Fürth, Braunschweig, Dresden L

Terms to push for:

Term Ask for Tag
Monthly fee Zero L
Wage share Start at 0 to 20% for a player on £5K p/w or more; accept up to about £2K to £3K p/w for a starter; pay all of it only when the wage is under £2K p/w L
Playing time Promise it only where true. Young players weigh game time more heavily in FM27 C
Recall clause Parent clubs want one. The AI recalls a little less readily in FM27 C
Optional future fee Ask for one on anyone you might keep. It costs nothing now L
Length The full season L

Stuttgart and Hoffenheim have reserve sides in your division, so they have less reason to lend to you L.

January and next summer

At a glance

  • Two kinds of pre-contract. Deals ending December 31, 2026 can be offered on day one and the player arrives on January 1, 2027. Deals ending June 30, 2027 can be approached from January and arrive on July 1, 2027. Both are likely, not confirmed L.
  • Dadiani is the one to do on day one. Kociubinski and Escudero are the other two worth an offer.
  • From January, call Harres first, then Großer and Lotka. They are signings for a promoted Fortuna, so offer wages from the next division's scale.
  • The Japanese group is the best-value pressing talent in the database: twelve players rated 63 to 68 on £900 to £4.2K p/w, all out of contract on June 30, 2027.
  • Renew Oberdorf before January, or another club can do to you what you are doing to them.

How to negotiate at this level

At a glance

  • No source publishes what a free agent wants. Every ask in this section is an estimate built from your own wage scale U. Approach the agent first to learn the real number L.
  • Your ceiling is what Hendrix and Oberdorf earn: £4.2K p/w C. Only one top-of-scale signing should go above it.
  • Keep the basic wage low and pay in things that cost money only when they happen: appearances, goals, promotion.
  • Sign the four you cannot do without in week one. Come back to the rest in the last week of the window and again in September.
  • The plan assumes at most three non-EU players in the matchday 20 U. If your rules screen shows no cap, the market gets much wider.

Where the estimates come from:

FMInside rating Estimated ask U Use
50 to 54 £0.7K to £1.8K p/w Cover or a youngster
55 to 57 £1.5K to £3K p/w Can start
58 to 61 £2.5K to £5K p/w Starter; near the top of your scale
62 or more £3.5K p/w and up Above the division. Possible only when his potential is 63 to 66, a modest name and not a faded star

The only hard anchors are five unattached players for whom FMInside happens to show a wage figure C: Sakai £4.3K p/w (rating 57), Datković £3.5K (59), Morales £2.6K (59), Albarracín £2.6K (59), Boutayeb £1.7K (58). Last real-life wages can be far higher (Stenzel about £25K p/w, Teuchert about £19K L), which is why those two are Possible and not Likely.

Clauses that keep the weekly wage down. The items exist in FM27 C; how far each moves the demand is carried over from older editions L.

Clause Use it on Why Tag
Appearance fee Kilian, Lenz, Marco John, Ajayi and other cover Low basic wage; you pay when he plays. Not for nailed-on starters, where it gets expensive C exists, L effect
Promotion wage rise, 15 to 25% Everyone you want next year: N'Diaye, Beifus, Kwateng, Gondo, Braga Lowers today's demand and is paid from a bigger budget C exists, L effect
Goal and clean-sheet bonuses Gondo, Braga, Fraisl Paid on output in place of basic wage C exists, L effect
One year plus a club option The 32- and 33-year-olds: Fraisl, Williams, Lemos, Ramalho, Dijks, Hamel Keep the good ones, shed the rest C exists, L effect
Lower squad status Bruijn, El Sheiwi, van Axel Dongen, Maku A lower promised status lowers the wage. A broken promise costs morale L
Signing-on and agent fees Sparingly They trade a one-off cost for a lower wage, but came from the bank balance in older editions. Check the balance first L
Relegation release clause Give it away when asked It does not matter if you go up L
Minimum-fee release clause Refuse for Ramos, van Axel Dongen, Maku, N'Diaye and anyone under 23 It caps your profit on the players with resale value. If forced, set it at three to four times his value L
Yearly wage rise Avoid It compounds on a long deal C

How to run a negotiation:

Step Do Tag
Before the offer Approach the agent to learn his interest and the wage he expects L
In the offer Lock the wage at your ceiling and let the agent move the other items L
For a name with hidden numbers Offer a trial: Friedrich, Challouk, Randall Rodríguez. Trials are not confirmed for FM27 U
For an injury doubt Read the scout report's wording on injury proneness before you sign: Kilian, Lenz and John first L
If he says no Leave him. Free agents' demands have historically fallen the longer they wait L
Contract length Three years with an option for the under-23s you could sell; one or two years for anyone over 28 L

The non-EU assumption and what changes without it. No source read for this guide confirms a cap on non-EU players in the 3. Liga, and older editions showed three in the matchday squad U. The plan is built to survive a cap of three:

If the rules screen shows Then
A cap of three in the 20 Keep the plan as written. N'Diaye, Braga and Gondo take the three places; Maku trains outside the 20; Dadiani rotates in from January, and one of the four sits out each week
A cap lower than three Swap Braga for Challouk (Belgian) or Teuchert (German), and treat Dadiani as cover for Hendrix only
No cap Swap Bruijn for Jhosefer and add Seb Ferdinand. Mbaizo, Gruezo, Ditta, Rubio, Ojo and Sow stop costing you a place, and the Japanese group in January becomes a straight choice on quality
The under-23 rule worded as German-only Ramos, van Axel Dongen and El Sheiwi no longer count. Rely on Lord and Arden, check Slimani, and keep two of Eixler, Meiser, Anhari and N. Egouli in the 20. See Signing and league rules

Germany has no work-permit system, so any nationality can sign; a non-EU player must be 18 to join from abroad L. Beifus, Wurm and Nunoo have no nationality on FMInside, so read theirs in game before you count them either way.

Wonderkids you can afford

At a glance

  • The famous wonderkids will not come to a third-tier club with £0 to spend. Your best prospect is one you already own: Elias Arden.
  • Outside the club, "wonderkid" here means a free agent or expiring contract aged 21 or under, rated 45-57 by FMInside, on roughly £0.5K-£2.5K p/w.
  • Do two things on day one: offer Nikoloz Dadiani a pre-contract, and approach the agents of van Axel Dongen, Maku and Seb Ferdinand.
  • Several names the research reports loved turned out weaker, or not free, once the real numbers were read. They are listed so you do not chase them.
  • Every wage ask is an estimate U. Every attribute, rating, wage and contract date from the database is C.

Player numbers are from FMInside's FM27 database (27.0.0, data patch 27.1.0), read on November 24, 2026 C. Verdicts (Likely, Possible, Long shot) come from the realism review of every name against Fortuna's wage scale: Likely means he should say yes at a wage that fits, Possible means expect a haggle or a no, Long shot means ask once and plan without him.

What "wonderkid" means at this level

At a glance

  • FMInside's rating and potential are its own 0-99 scale. They are not Football Manager's 0-200 current and potential ability.
  • On that scale Fortuna's best players are 57-60, a 3. Liga starter is about 54, and 62 or more is above the division.
  • "Dynamic potential" means the game rolls the player's potential inside a band in every new save. He can be a star in one save and ordinary in the next.
  • So scout for what you can see: running numbers, Determination, age, and your own scouts' star range.
  • Exact game ability is published for one Fortuna player only: Arden.

The honest picture. The transfer budget is £0 and about £11K p/w of wages is free C. Free agents rated 62 or more last earned far above Fortuna's scale. FM Scout's own free-agent list warns that it is graded for top-flight sides and that those players may not want a lower-league club C. The players below are the ones who are both good enough to grow and likely to say yes.

Number you see What it is How to use it Details
FMInside rating The site's 0-99 estimate of how good he is now 55-61 can start in the 3. Liga; 50-54 is cover or a youngster; under 50 is a project Tag: C for the number, the bands are the realism review's rule of thumb; Fortuna yardstick: Hendrix and Oberdorf 60, Heintz 59
FMInside potential The site's 0-99 estimate of his ceiling A fixed number such as 65 or 75 will be the same in every save Tag: C; Example: Maku 45 now, 75 potential, the highest fixed potential of any free agent in the data
"Dynamic" potential Potential is randomised when the save is created Treat it as "unknown, could be high". Let your scouts' star range decide Tag: C that it is randomised; the band for each player is not published, except Arden's
FM Scout "R" A 1-100 recommendation score on FM Scout's lists Kept only where the research quoted it. Never compare it with an FMInside rating Tag: C; FM Scout's wonderkid list covers players it says have potential 150+ on the game's 0-200 scale
Wage ask An estimate Approach the agent first and read the real demand Tag: U; built from the five free agents whose last wage the data shows: a 57-59 player asked £1.7K-£4.3K p/w

Randomised potential, using Arden. FM Scout publishes his exact numbers: current ability 102 and a potential code of -85, which the game turns into a random figure between 140 and 170 in each save C. FMInside shows the same thing as "51, dynamic". The other codes are -9 (150-180), -95 (160-190) and -10 (170-200) C. For every other "dynamic" player in this section the band is not published; check in game.

Loans as development

At a glance

  • No source shows who is loan-listed or what share of a wage a parent club pays. Every line is a request to try, not a plan U.
  • You already hold three loans (Rieß, Müller, Bornschein). A cap of about six is expected, with under-21s possibly exempt U.
  • Young players at bigger clubs are mostly rated 45-55, so a loan adds depth and under-23 bodies, not starters.
  • Your offer is the one thing bigger clubs cannot match: a truthful promise of regular football.
  • Best three to ask for: Jordana (Girona B), Grothe (Hertha BSC), Hawighorst (Bayer 04 U19).

What to offer. Promise the playing time you can really give: young players weigh promised minutes more heavily in FM27, and a broken promise costs more C. Open with a small wage share and no loan fee; parent clubs usually ask little of a third-tier club that guarantees starts L. Ask for an option to buy where a release clause is small (Jordana, Peries). AI managers recall loans a little less readily in FM27 C. Post what you need on TransferRoom, which is in FM27 C; how requirements are posted follows the FM26 workflow L.

How to grow them

At a glance

  • Minutes come first. The 3. Liga is the right level for your best teenagers, so play them in the first team where they also fill under-23 places.
  • The three tactic stages are a ladder: a youngster who clears the stage 1 minimums for his slot plays now, and the stage 2 and 3 minimums are his training targets.
  • Fortuna II is in the fifth tier in real life. That is fine for 16-17-year-olds and too weak for anyone close to the first team.
  • Put Arden and the best newcomer with Hendrix or Oberdorf on the Mentoring tab. How its groups work in FM27 is U.
  • Sell late and with clauses: a percentage of the next sale, and a buy-back on anyone under 20.

Where each type plays. Ratings are FMInside's.

Finding more

At a glance

Money and wages

At a glance

  • Fortuna has a second-tier crowd and third-tier income. The gate is your edge; television money is the prize.
  • Each promotion multiplies central income: about £1.1M in the 3. Liga, £6M to £8M in the 2. Bundesliga, £27M to £35M in the Bundesliga.
  • In window one, three exits (Zimmermann, Förster, Schleusener) turn £11,000 p/w of wage room into £29,345 p/w.
  • Pay with clauses, not basic wage: appearance fees, a promotion rise of 15 to 25%, sell-on percentages instead of fees.
  • There is no owner to bail you out. Under 50+1 every pound comes from results, the crowd or a sale.

Day-one budgets are in The club on day one. Real-world money figures are for 2026/27 and are tagged L because Football Manager 27's own television and prize figures are not published U. Anything marked "planning figure" is my estimate, not a game fact.

Where the money comes from

At a glance

  • Four streams: the gate, television, the DFB-Pokal and sponsorship. Player sales are the fifth once you have someone to sell.
  • At this level the gate is the biggest of them and television the smallest.
  • One DFB-Pokal win is worth more than a season of spare wages.
  • Read the Finances income screen in the first week: none of the in-game amounts are published.
Stream At the start Tag
Gate The 53,500 ground is the largest in the division C. In real life: 19,000 season tickets and a 31,362 average, about three times the league mean C / L
Gate estimate Crowd x home games x ticket price. Example only: 31,000 x 19 x an assumed £10.40 net is about £6.1M a season. The price is an assumption U
Television About £1.14M a season in real life, an equal share for each of the 18 first teams; reserve sides get nothing L
DFB-Pokal £184K for playing round one in real life; gate split evenly, and third-tier clubs play at home L
Sponsorship No totals published. In the series it comes in fixed-term deals that scale with division and reputation U / L
Player sales Team value £12M C. The share of a fee you keep is not published C / U
Stadium rent A cost, not income: reported at about £1.3M a year in real life after the city halved it L

Three things move the gate L: results in the first two months (third-tier crowds fall with form), cup ties against bigger clubs, and promotion. In the top two divisions there are 17 home league games instead of 19, but a sold-out Bundesliga season is about 910,000 tickets against roughly 596,000 now.

Income by division

At a glance

  • The jump from the 3. Liga to the 2. Bundesliga is five to seven times the television money.
  • The jump to the Bundesliga is four times that again.
  • Inside each division the share rises the longer you stay, so the first season after promotion is the leanest.
  • Champions League entry alone pays more than half a promoted Bundesliga club's television income.

Wage structure by division

At a glance

  • One rule at every level: wage bill near 55 to 65% of income, top earner near 6 to 8% of the wage budget.
    1. Liga: £128K p/w in total; keep the top earner to £7K to £9K (Zimmermann, on £10.0K, is already above it).
  • Each promotion roughly doubles or triples the total. Raise the bands only as far as the new budget allows.
  • The first two rows rest on the game's published budgets. The last two are planning figures: check them against what the board gives you.
  • Keep the structure flat. One outlier contract becomes the number every renewal is measured against.

Freeing wage room in the first window

At a glance

  • You start with about £11K p/w spare. That is two modest signings.
  • Move on Zimmermann (once a right-back is in), Förster and Schleusener and you have £29,345 p/w: enough for the twelve free agents in The rebuild.
  • If clubs take Sauck, van der Sloot, Gerezgiher and Consbruch it reaches £43,733 p/w; sending Rieß back to Mainz adds up to £6,670 more. Treat both as a bonus.
  • Sell or loan with the wage covered. A release costs a pay-off from a balance you have not seen yet.
  • Keep about £3K p/w back for January.

Contract tactics that save money

At a glance

  • Offer a lower basic wage and pay the difference in things that only cost money when they happen.
  • Promotion rise of 15 to 25% for everyone you want to keep: it costs nothing unless income has multiplied.
  • One or two-year deals with a club option for anyone over 28; longer deals only for under-23s you could sell.
  • Refuse minimum-fee release clauses on young players, or set them at three times his value.
  • When you sell, take a sell-on percentage. When you buy with no budget, offer one instead of a fee.

When you sign or renew:

Clause Use Why Tag
Appearance fee Back-ups, older free agents, injury risks You pay only when he plays. Costly for an ever-present, so not for nailed-on starters C exists, L effect
Goal and clean-sheet bonuses In place of basic wage Paid on output C exists, L effect
Promotion wage rise, 15 to 25% Everyone you want next year Lowers today's demand; paid from a budget that should roughly double C exists, L effect
