When you sell, loan or buy:

Tool Use Tag
Sell-on clause when selling Always ask for one. For a prospect it can be worth more than the fee L
Sell-on percentage instead of a fee when buying Offer the selling club a share of the next sale; your transfer budget is £0 L
Instalments Spread a fee over two or three seasons U for FM27
Loans in: monthly fee Offer zero L
Loans in: wage contribution Start at 0 to 20% for a player on £5K p/w or more. Accept up to about £2K to £3K p/w for a starter. Pay 100% only when the wage is under £2K p/w L
Loans in: optional future fee Ask for one on anyone you might keep. It costs nothing now L
Loans out Ask the other club to pay the whole wage L
Pre-contracts Sign expiring players in January for nothing in the summer L

Loan limits L: the scheme used in Germany caps professionals on loan in and out in a season (six each way, three with any one club), with under-21s and club-trained players exempt. Keep loans to a minority of the XI anyway: they all leave in June.

What to ask the board for, and when

At a glance

  • Day one: a senior affiliate and a coaching course. Both are cheap for the board.
  • After a cup win or a strong autumn: a wage budget top-up.
  • The week after promotion: training and youth facilities, then youth recruitment and junior coaching.
  • Never: the stadium. The city owns it.
  • One request at a time; a refusal starts a cooldown.
When Ask for Why then Tag
First week Senior affiliate that lends players Free loans; costs the board nothing L
First week Coaching course for you The board pays L
First month An extra coach or scout slot, if the cap is tight In real life more than half the staff left, so the allowed numbers may be thin. Each wage comes from your spare budget L
After a DFB-Pokal win, a sale or a strong autumn Wage budget increase A one-off top-up; the board may give less than you ask L
Promotion secured Training facilities, then youth facilities The board is happy and television money is about to jump L
First 2. Bundesliga season Youth recruitment, junior coaching, more scouts, a lower-league affiliate for your loans Fortuna II may still be too low for your best prospects L
Bundesliga A facility request every time a cooldown ends; staff slots to the division maximum; a foreign scouting affiliate Income supports it L
Champions League years Facilities to 20; stadium expansion Expect "no" on the stadium while the city owns it L / U

Also use the budget slider with care [C exists, rate U]: with £0 to spend, the only direction on day one is wages into fees, and you have little wage room to give.

Financial traps

At a glance

  • Promotion rises land together in July. Add them up before the last game of the season.
  • No sugar daddy: under 50+1 there is no takeover and no debt cleared for you.
  • Relegation halves television money. Put wage-drop clauses in Bundesliga contracts for the first two years.
  • Do not spend the whole wage budget in July, and do not build the XI out of loans.
  • Read the balance and any loan repayment before you promise anyone a signing-on fee.
Trap What happens Guard Tag
Promotion wage rises Every rise lands at once. On today's £117K p/w, 25% across the board is about £29K p/w more Read each contract's rise before the last game; keep rises at 25% or less; no promotion bonus you cannot afford L
Ageing promotion heroes Rising wages for falling legs One-year deals with a club option after 28 L
Relegation clauses Players and agents ask for a relegation release clause. Real second-tier contracts at Fortuna lapsed on relegation Concede it now; from the Bundesliga add a relegation wage drop to every deal for two years L
50+1 No tycoon takeover at a member-owned German club Plan every budget from league place, cup runs, the crowd and sales L
Spending it all in July Nothing left for January or for an injury Keep about £3K p/w back now; 10% of the wage budget from the 2. Bundesliga L
Too many loanees They leave in June and the squad must be rebuilt again. Müller, Rieß and Bornschein already do Loans as a minority of the XI; ask for future-fee options L
Selling before you know the percentage You may keep well under 100% of a fee Read the share on Finances first U
Selling prospects early Arden's fee now is a fraction of his later worth No small-fee sales in window one; take sell-on clauses if you must L
Low release clauses A bigger club removes your say No higher-division or Champions League-club clause, ever L
The promotion windfall Fees and five-year contracts that a relegation cannot carry Wage bill at 55 to 65% of income; short deals for older players L
Insolvency In real life it costs nine points in the 3. Liga. Whether the game runs the DFB's licence check is doubtful Avoid a deep negative balance L
Squad Cost Ratio FM27 has the rule; scope and penalties are not published. Nothing suggests it applies in the 3. Liga Check the rules screen now and again on reaching Europe C / U
A season without the Champions League A wage bill sized for it breaches the cost rule Size wages to Bundesliga income; treat Europe as the bonus L

The 3. Liga

At a glance

  • You are the biggest club in the division by reputation, stadium and crowd, with the second-largest wage budget. Your squad is valued only eighth.
  • Four clubs are real promotion rivals: Duisburg, Rostock, Essen and Aachen. Münster and Saarbrücken are the outsiders.

At a glance

Road to glory

At a glance

  • Six phases take you from the 3. Liga to a Champions League win. The fast path is about ten to twelve seasons, the slow one fifteen to twenty (planning figure U).
  • Money arrives before reputation does. At every level the wall is who will talk to you, so young players, loans and your own academy are the way through it L.
  • There is no takeover money under 50+1. Promotions, crowds, cup runs, prize money and player sales pay for everything L.
  • Each phase below gives the aim, the squad level, the tactic stage, what to buy first, what to ask the board for and the usual mistake.
  • Almost every board, reputation and facility mechanic here is carried from FM26 L. Note what your own save does the first time each one comes up.

The season ranges come from two paths in the road report, an ambitious one and a cautious one. Both are planning figures U, not measured averages.

Phase 1: the 3. Liga

At a glance

  • Aim: promotion in season one. Top two go up, third plays the 2. Bundesliga's 16th over two legs, the bottom four go down L.
  • Squad level: FMInside rating 54+ makes a 3. Liga starter; your best are 57-60; 62+ is above the level and usually above the wage C.
  • Tactic: Front Foot. Move to Swarm when the front six finish games with energy to spare.
  • Spend first on wages for free agents, inside £11K p/w of spare budget C. There is no transfer budget C.
  • Classic mistake: spending the whole wage budget in July and leaving nothing for January.

Why go at once: Fortuna have the top reputation in the division C, the second-highest wage budget C and the largest stadium C. Every extra third-tier season costs about £5.0M to £6.7M in television money alone, on real 2026/27 figures L.

What to spend on first:

  1. The spine of the XI on free transfers, signed early in the window so cohesion can build C.
  2. Loans from Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs, with honest playing-time promises. Keep loanees to a minority of the XI: they leave in June L.
  3. Empty staff slots filled with free agents. Each wage comes out of the same £11K p/w L.

What to ask the board for:

When Request Details
First month A senior affiliate that lends players Best odds: it costs the board nothing L. Whether a Bundesliga club will be asked is U
First month A coaching course for yourself Cheap; the board pays L
First month Extra coach and scout slots Fair odds L. In real life more than half the club's staff left in summer 2026, so the allowed numbers may be thin L
After a good autumn or a cup win Junior coaching, then youth recruitment Often the cheapest youth upgrades L
Once promotion is secure Training and youth facilities, once Probably refused before then: the board has no cash L

Contracts: one-year or two-year deals with a club option for older free agents, longer deals for anyone under 23 you could sell L. Offer a promotion wage rise of 15% to 25% in place of a higher basic wage, and no more than about 25% L. Read every promotion wage rise before the last game of the season: they all land together in July L.

Mistake What it costs Details
Spending the whole wage budget in July Nothing left for January Hold some back
Too many loanees A second rebuild next summer In real life FIFA's loan caps (six in, six out, three with one club) apply in Germany; under-21s are exempt L
Ignoring the under-23 rule A starter left off the sheet Four must be named, not played L
A cup run on a thin squad Tired legs in a 38-game season Use the five substitutes

Phase 2: the 2. Bundesliga

At a glance

  • Aim: top half in year one, top three in year two or three. Top two go up; third plays the Bundesliga's 16th L.
  • Squad level: no FMInside band is published for this division. Use wages as the yardstick: the median wage budget is about £213K p/w C.
  • Tactic: Swarm. Staying on it for a whole season here does no harm.
  • Spend first on five to seven upgrades, then on 19-23-year-olds you can sell.
  • Classic mistake: promotion wage rises and ageing promotion heroes eating the new budget.

Why not rush: a promoted club gets £6.1M to £7.8M of television money against £17.4M to £20.9M for clubs just relegated from the Bundesliga, on real 2026/27 figures L. The gap inside this division is larger than the gap at the bottom of the Bundesliga. One season to rebuild is the normal price.

Area Plan Details
Aim Year one: top half Bottom two go down; 16th plays the 3. Liga's third L
Squad level Not published; check in game FMInside bands for this division are not in the reports. Compare each target's wage with the division's: an implied average first-team wage of about £8.5K p/w L
Wage budget needed £170K to £200K p/w to survive £240K+ p/w to compete at the top L. Your £128K p/w today would rank 16th of 18 here C
Likely wage budget £200K to £300K p/w Planning figure L, from income. Top earner about £15K to £20K p/w
Tactic stage Swarm Move to Heavy Metal when two centre-backs have Pace and Acceleration in the low-to-mid teens and the goalkeeper sweeps. It depends on centre-back pace more than on the league
Turnover Five to seven in, first summer Players who carried you up are usually good enough as squad players for a year

What to spend on first:

  1. The slots where the promotion side strained most. Use the Swarm minimums in "Three tactics, one identity".
  2. 19-23-year-olds for small fees from the 3. Liga, Regionalliga, Austria, Switzerland, the Dutch second tier, Scandinavia and Poland. Sell one a year to a Bundesliga club L.
  3. More Bundesliga loans.

The first real transfer money arrives here: day-one transfer budgets in this division run from about £90K to £4.3M, with a typical club on £260K to £430K C.

Mistake What to do instead Details

Phase 3: Bundesliga survival

At a glance

  • Aim: 15th or better in year one. 16th is a play-off; 17th and 18th go down L.
  • Squad level: not published as an FMInside band. The cheapest Bundesliga wage budget on day one is £346K p/w and the median is about £800K p/w C.
  • Tactic: Heavy Metal where the squad can run it, Swarm against sides that will counter you.
  • Spend first on six to eight signings and on relegation-proof contracts.
  • Classic mistake: blowing the promotion windfall on fees and five-year deals. Relegation halves television income.
Area Plan Details
Aim Stay up Then mid-table, 8th to 12th, in years two and three
Money £27.0M to £34.8M television money Real 2026/27 range for promoted clubs L. Plus full houses
Wage budget £600K to £800K p/w Planning figure L, from income. Top earner about £35K to £50K p/w
Tactic stage Heavy Metal It carries the heaviest physical cost in the game. Signs of strain: one long ball beats eight players; the team fades after 60 to 70 minutes
Turnover Six to eight in After that, three to five a year
Registration Local Player rule 12 German-licensed players under contract; 8 locally trained, of whom 4 club-trained L. Read the rules screen on promotion

What to spend on first: pace at centre-back and running power at full-back, because Heavy Metal leaves space behind both. Then finishing in the front three, which acts on goals in community testing C. Passing and Decisions showed almost no in-match value in the same tests C, so do not overpay for pure technicians.

What to ask the board for: training and youth facilities, one level every time a cooldown ends, with 17+ as the target for the Bundesliga years L. Staff slots up to the division maximum L. A foreign scouting affiliate once you can pay fees L.

Mistake What to do instead Details
Over-spending the windfall Relegation wage-drop clauses in every contract for two years Relegation halves television income L

Phase 4: Bundesliga top six

At a glance

  • Aim: 5th to 7th and a cup run. Europe comes by league place or by winning the DFB-Pokal.
  • Squad level: an established mid-table side on £1.0M to £1.3M p/w in wages (planning figure L).
  • Tactic: Heavy Metal as the default, with two players for the hardest-running slots.
  • Spend first on 18-22-year-olds you can sell at a large profit, and on 16-18-year-olds who start the club-trained clock.
  • Classic mistake: Thursday football on a thin squad costing league points.

What to ask the board for: youth recruitment and junior coaching up to the top bands L. A commercial affiliate once you are in Europe L. Stadium expansion only after a full sold-out season, and expect a no while the city owns the ground U.

Mistake What to do instead Details

Phase 5: Champions League regular

At a glance

  • Aim: top four every season, a DFB-Pokal, then the title against Bayern, Dortmund, Leverkusen and Leipzig.
  • Squad level: first-team-ready 21-24-year-olds alongside the prospects you developed.
  • Tactic: Heavy Metal. The squad should now meet its numbers in every slot.
  • Spend first on keeping your stars: renew two years before expiry.
  • Classic mistake: breaching the Squad Cost Ratio after one season without the Champions League.
Area Plan Details
Aim Top four, then the title Domestic television money at the top is £57M to £80M in real life L
Champions League entry At least £16.2M before a ball is kicked Plus the value pillar. More than half a promoted Bundesliga club's television income L
A last-16 run with four wins About £37M to £39M Arithmetic from the real prize table, before the value pillar L
Wage limit The squad cost rule In real life UEFA limits wages, amortised fees and agent fees to 70% of revenue plus sale profit L. FM27 added Squad Cost Ratio rules C; which competitions carry it and the penalties are U
Squad model Sell at most one starter a summer At your price, with the replacement already signed
Turnover Two to four a year 22-24 senior players plus List B youngsters

What to ask the board for: training and youth facilities to 20 L. Data and sports-science departments if FM27 lets you ask U. Stadium expansion L.

Keeping stars, most useful first L:

  1. Renew two years before expiry for anyone you could sell at a profit.
  2. Never agree a "higher division" or "Champions League club" clause.
  3. Promise only what you can deliver. A broken promise does more damage than a refused transfer.
  4. When a giant bids, either take a price that funds two replacements or reject it and talk to the player the same day.
  5. Keep loyal, professional team leaders in the squad. Dressing-room support limits unrest.
  6. Sell a year early: a 27-28-year-old star with two years left is at peak price.

Bayern take players three ways: a release clause, an unsettled player after a rejected bid, or a contract inside its last 18 months L. FM27's AI recruitment was reworked C, so expect richer clubs to move earlier on young Bundesliga performers L.

The mistakes at this level: an ageing core that won the first trophies; one or two outlier contracts that every renewal is then measured against; a wage bill that only works with Champions League money.

Phase 6: Champions League winner

At a glance

  • Aim: quarter-finals as the norm, then win it.
  • Squad level: two players for every slot on the tactic's profile, with elite 17-19-year-olds now choosing you.
  • Tactic: Heavy Metal, rotated hard. Knockout ties are variance; depth is the answer.
  • Spend first on depth, and on renewing a whole generation before its contracts end together.
  • Classic mistake: letting the league slip. The Champions League place funds everything.
Area Plan Details
Aim Win the Champions League A deep run pays about £52M to £87M or more; winning it pays well over £87M in prize money on the way through, on real 2026/27 figures L
Reputation Top band comes last It should reach the top band only after a final or a win L
Registration Club-trained players fill the quota So that all 17 free List A places hold top players L
Turnover One or two starters a year
First draw Expect a hard one The club coefficient is built over five seasons and sets the seeding pot; a new club starts at the bottom L

Locally trained At most 4 of the 8 association-trained Association-trained: three seasons at any German club between 15 and 21. The rest must be club-trained: three seasons at Fortuna between 15 and 21

List B Unlimited Under-21s with two unbroken years at the club since turning 15
Nationality Irrelevant A Brazilian who joins at 17 and stays three seasons is club-trained

Target for the first Champions League season: four club-trained players good enough for the bench and four more German-trained players in the 25 L.

The mistakes at this level: one XI and no depth; a whole generation's contracts ending in the same summer; complacency in the league.

Reputation

At a glance

  • Reputation is a hidden number per club, shown as a band and a star rating L. Yours is the highest in the 3. Liga on day one C.
  • It decides which players and staff will talk to you. This is the main wall on the whole climb L.
  • It rises slowly and in jumps: promotions, finishes above expectation, trophies and, above all, European results L.
  • Speed it up with cup runs, back-to-back promotions and any European football, even the Conference League.
  • Your own reputation as manager grows with time and results; the coaching course is the one thing you can ask for L.
Point How it works Details
What it is A hidden number, shown as a band FM26 players describe the bands running National, then Continental L
What raises it Winning Promotions, league finishes above expectation, trophies and continental results. League and cup reputation feed the club figure L
How fast Slow and lumpy One FM26 player sat at National through years of top-half finishes and European places, then moved to Continental straight after winning the Champions League. No source gives a rate L
What it gates Players and staff A player weighs your reputation against his own, plus the division, the playing time and the wage L
What it may also feed Sponsorship, season tickets, friendlies, affiliates, board requests U
Your edge now Top of the division 3. Liga-level and many 2. Bundesliga-level players should listen L

Getting round the wall L:

  • Young players with low reputation and high potential join clubs that established players refuse.
  • Loans from bigger clubs depend less on your reputation than permanent deals do. Playing-time promises matter more, and they weigh more for young players in FM27 C.
  • Staff apply the same test. Good coaches without a job are the obtainable ones.

Speeding it up:

Lever Why it works Details
DFB-Pokal runs Cup reputation feeds the club figure L In real life clubs from the 3. Liga and below are always drawn at home L. Field the strongest XI in round one
Promotion, twice Each one is a finish above expectation The division's own reputation counts too L
Any European football Continental results move reputation most L A Conference League season pays little but builds the name and the coefficient
Your own badges Ask for the coaching course at once L Your standing with the board rests on time at the club and your own reputation L

Manager reputation: no report gives FM27 mechanics beyond the two points above. Not published; check your profile at each milestone. Note the club's star rating and band each time something big happens, and you will build your own rate-of-rise data.

Youth and the second team

At a glance

  • The intake arrives once a year. Its quality rests on Germany's youth rating, your youth recruitment, youth facilities, junior coaching and the Head of Youth Development L.
  • With mid-table ratings expect one or two useful newgens a year and a real prospect only now and then L.
  • Fortuna II play in the Oberliga Niederrhein, the fifth tier, in real life L. That is fine for 16-17-year-olds and too weak for anyone close to first-team level L.
  • So the 3. Liga is your loan: play the best teenagers in the first team, where they also fill the under-23 places.
  • The German intake date is not confirmed for FM27 U. Put the Head of Youth Development in post in week one.

Selling to grow

At a glance

  • The model: sign cheap or free at 17-21, give real minutes, sell after one or two good seasons, and take a share of the next sale.
  • Value follows the club's division and reputation as much as ability, so every promotion raises the price of everyone you own L.
  • Cash in when the fee funds two replacements, or a year before a contract or a body runs down.
  • Do not sell your best prospects for small fees in window one. A sell-on clause is the better tool.
  • In FM27 scout reports show an existing sell-on clause, and a club that owes one asks for more C.

  • Champions League entry alone is worth at least £16.2M and is the step that changes the wage structure L.

Spoilers

At a glance

  • These are the long-run mechanics that decide a ten-season save. Most are carried from FM26 or older editions L; the match-engine findings are FM27 community tests C.
  • Athletes win in this engine: Acceleration and Pace first, then Jumping Reach, Stamina, Anticipation and Work Rate C.
  • Rotation, familiarity and cohesion are worth more points than any single instruction C.
  • The Head of Youth Development shapes the personality and positions of every intake L.
  • Reputation moves in jumps, and the biggest jump comes from European results L.

The match engine, from one set of FM27 community tests with fixed seeds C. It is the best early evidence, not settled fact.

When it goes wrong

At a glance

  • A failed promotion is normal: in real life only 11 of 49 relegated clubs went straight back up L. The plan allows two seasons.
  • If the board will not invest, use the levers that cost nothing: the Head of Youth Development, affiliates, staff slots and sales.
  • Board patience is not published U. The real board dismissed its head coach ten league games into 2026/27 L, so do not assume a long leash.
  • Hold back 10% of the wage budget at every level (planning figure U) so a bad autumn can be fixed in January.
  • When results dip, go back a tactic stage before you change anything else.

A failed promotion:

Step What to do Details
Secure the floor Finish top four It keeps the DFB-Pokal place for next season L. Whether the regional cup is in the game is U
Count the cost About £5.0M to £6.7M of television money lost L The 3. Liga share rises a little from 2027/28 L
Protect the squad Keep the core; change three or four The loanees leave in June, which is why they should be a minority of the XI L
Use the contracts Club options on one-year and two-year deals Promotion wage rises cost nothing if you stay down L
Sell one A developed player with a sell-on clause It funds the second attempt
Reset the target Negotiate the league expectation down a step if Club Vision offers it L

A board that will not invest:

Situation What to do Details
Facility request refused Wait for a promotion or a cup upset, then ask again A refusal starts a random cooldown L
A smaller counter-offer Take it L
No money at all Ask for what is free A senior affiliate, a coaching course, staff slots L
A board cold on youth Lean on signings at 16-18 and on loans Board character cannot be changed L
Budget stuck Move money with the slider on Finances FM27 lets you shift money between transfer and wage budgets C; rate and limits U
Still stuck Talk up growth in press conferences A small nudge L

A sacking risk:

Signal What to do Details
A bad run in a promotion season Drop a tactic stage and rotate Condition and familiarity are worth more than instructions C
The expectation is promotion and you are mid-table at the winter break Use the held-back wages in January The winter break runs to about 01/14/2027 in real life L
The board is unhappy Do not make a request It wastes a cooldown L
Players unsettled Keep promises small and keep them A broken promise does more damage than a refused transfer L
An overloaded squad Stop buying Cohesion is worth 0.2 to 0.3 points a game C

In the Bundesliga years the same logic holds with bigger numbers. Relegation halves television income L, so the relegation wage-drop clauses from Phase 2 and Phase 3 are what make a bad season survivable. After a season without the Champions League, cut the wage bill before the Squad Cost Ratio does it for you U.

Day-one checklist

At a glance

  • Work down the list in order and tick each item as you go. Each line names the person, setting or screen, and the section it comes from.
  • Everything up to the end of "First hour" happens before you press Continue for the first time.
  • Read before you act: the Finances and rules screens decide how far the signing list can go.
  • Approach replacement staff before you end anyone's contract, and sell before you sign past the first four.
  • Later phases are reminders for the season. Tick them when they come up.

Before the first click

At a glance

  • Three things before you touch any screen in the new career.
  • The board's expectation is shown when you pick the club and is not published anywhere.
  • Nothing on this list needs advice on leagues, database or hardware: that set-up is yours.

First hour: screens, staff and board

At a glance

  • Read the screens in the first block before any offer. They answer the top five Open questions.
  • Then the staff offers, in the order given: fitness, goalkeeping, physio and youth come first.
  • One board request at a time. A refusal starts a cooldown.
  • ☐
    1. Liga > Rules > Squad Selection: under-23 wording, number and cut-off; any non-EU cap; bench size and substitutions (Signing and league rules).
  • ☐
    1. Liga > Rules > Transfers and Dates: loan limits, winter window, play-off dates (Signing and league rules).
  • ☐
    1. Liga > Rules > Prize Money, and DFB-Pokal > Rules: in-game payouts (Signing and league rules; Money and wages).

First window: exits, signings, loans and pre-contracts

At a glance

  • Signings go in the order The rebuild gives, so the list still works if you have to stop early.
  • The first four fit inside the wage room you start with. The rest wait for exits.
  • If Zimmermann will not move, stop at eight signings. If nobody moves, stop at four.
  • The window shuts on September 1, 2026 at 8:00 pm local time L.

Pre-season: tactic, training and friendlies

At a glance

  • One tactic only: Front Foot, as the Primary Trained Tactic.
  • Set roles from the tactics board; no player instructions at stage 1.
  • The first two weeks are the heaviest physical load of the year.

First month

At a glance

  • The league starts away at Waldhof Mannheim on August 7, 2026; the cup follows two weeks later.
  • Rotation is the biggest lever for a pressing side.
  • Renew Oberdorf before another club can approach him.

January

At a glance

  • The winter break is the second pre-season and the best time to move up a stage, if the squad feels ready.
  • Dadiani arrives. Pre-contract talks for next summer open.
  • Read the winter window dates in game: they were not found for this season.

End of season

At a glance

  • Three midweek rounds in March and April are the only crowded weeks.
  • Add up the promotion wage rises before the last game.
  • Loans and expiring deals end on June 30, 2027; pre-contract signings arrive on July 1, 2027.

Open questions

At a glance

  • Every "check in game", unverified U line and unresolved source conflict from the nine sections, with duplicates merged.
  • The five that change the plan most are the cards at the top. Settle them in the first hour, before any offer.
  • The tables below follow the guide's order, one per section. Each row says where to look and what changes with the answer.
  • Click a row for the source conflict or the fallback.
  • When your screen and this guide differ, trust the screen.

Sources

At a glance

  • Nothing to do here; this is the reference list.
  • Player and staff numbers come from FMInside's FM27 database, read in a browser on November 24, 2026. Those pages are not linked.

  • Left out: pages the research agents could not open, pages a report marked as out of date or unused, and duplicate addresses.

How the research was done

At a glance

  • Four layers, in order of authority: the FMInside database, a realism review, ten research reports, and your own tactics screens for every role and instruction name.
  • Where the database and a report disagreed, the database won, and the section says so where it matters.
  • No source publishes an FM27 save that starts in the 3. Liga, so mechanics are mostly carried from FM26 or older editions and tagged L.

Research reports. Ten reports were written by research agents searching the web in November 2026: the squad, the club, the league, tactics, staff leadership, coaches, free agents and loans, cheap signings, wonderkids, and the road to glory. Each tagged its own claims; a real-world fact became L in this guide unless an FM27 source confirmed the game matches it.

The database. FMInside's FM27 database (27.0.0 with data patch 27.1.0) was read in a browser on November 24, 2026, for Fortuna's squad, every recommended signing and loan target, and every recommended staff member. Attribute numbers, wages, contract dates and FMInside's own 0-99 ratings come from there and are C. Euro wages were divided by 1.15. Staff wages are not in it.

Your own game. The tactics creator was read from your save on November 16, 2026: style, formation, role, instruction, option and screen names. Only names from that read appear in the guide.

Realism review. A separate review checked every recommended signing and hire against Fortuna's reputation, wage scale and the player's status, and gave each a verdict (Likely, Possible, Long shot, Stretch or Out). Its verdicts decided who made the recommended lists.

Earlier project files. The fact-checked Manchester United guide and its research supplied verified FM27 mechanics (transfers, training, Squad Cost Ratio, the FM-Arena match-engine findings) and the format. No United-specific content was reused.
